test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which statement shows interaction of an abiotic component with a biotic component in an ecosystem?

options.text: An earthworm making a burrow in the soil
Tap water running into a stream
Two birds fighting with each other for food
A frog feeding on a grasshopper

solution:
The correct answer is __**An earthworm making a burrow in the soil**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To understand the interaction between an abiotic component (non-living) and a biotic component (living) in an ecosystem, we must identify cases where living organisms interact with non-living parts of their environment.
 
• The interaction between an earthworm and the soil demonstrates a clear relationship between a biotic component (earthworm) and an abiotic component (soil) in the ecosystem.
 
• Biotic Component:
 
• The earthworm is a living organism. Biotic components in an ecosystem are organisms like plants, animals, fungi, and microorganisms.
 
• Abiotic Component:The soil is a non-living (abiotic) component. Abiotic components include things like air, water, soil, temperature, light, and minerals.
 
• The earthworm digs into the soil to create burrows.
 
• As it does so, it physically modifies the soil structure, affecting its aeration and water retention capacity.
 
• This interaction helps improve soil fertility by mixing organic material and promoting the decomposition of organic matter.
 
• In this process, the earthworm is relying on the soil for shelter and survival, while simultaneously benefiting the soil ecosystem.
